title: The Prince and the Painted Portrait

keywords: tale of the prince who fell in love with the picture
full_text:
Prince Farhad of Persia discovered in an ancient ivory cabinet an exquisitely painted miniature portrait of a maiden of breathtaking beauty. Captivated by the painted eyes, the prince neglected his studies, refused food, and vowed to travel the ends of the earth to find the living original.

After two years of wandering through India and China, he arrived at the court of the King of the White Isles, where he discovered that the original of the portrait was Princess Niloufar.

However, when he entered her presence, he was bitterly disappointed: the princess was proud, vain, spoke with cruel sarcasm to her servants, and cared only for her own reflection in mirrors!

Disillusioned and grieving, Farhad left the palace and walked through the city gardens. There he met Princess Niloufar’s younger sister, Princess Parisa, who was not portrayed in royal miniatures, but who spent her days reading books, nursing wounded birds, and managing schools for orphan children.

As they spoke, Farhad discovered a soul of sublime intelligence, gentle wit, and radiant compassion.

He realized his youthful folly: 'I chased a painted phantom of vanity, while the true pearl of the kingdom was walking quietly in the garden!'

Farhad sought Princess Parisa’s hand in marriage, celebrating a union founded on genuine character, proving that real beauty resides in the living virtues of the heart, not on painted parchment.
moral: Do not fall in love with a painted shadow; seek the living reality of character and virtue.
